newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac defends new China relationship.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac defends new China relationship.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac hailed on Friday a new economic and political relationship with China, saying this had not been achieved at the expense of human rights.

"In a very short time we have achieved substantial gains, the result of a strategy of exchange and cooperation," he said, citing China's decision to sign a United Nations covenant on social and economic rights and to consider signing a covenant on civil rights.
"This is happening at the very moment when we have adopted a strategy of consultation," he told a news conference when asked about human rights.
The deals worth about $1.8 billion signed on the first day of his four-day state visit to China on Thursday had guaranteed jobs for thousands of French workers, he said.

A communique signed to map out Sino-French relations would have important effects on political and economic ties, he said, describing it as "the most important political document signed between China and France since 1964".
